co_three_of_a_kind_wall.blurb: A small bouldering wall on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder, tucked in the Great Ridge section and reached by walking uphill past the Pebble Wall and Overhang Wall. It holds eleven problems, running from a very easy ledge line up to V5, with a cluster at V4 and V5 and a few gentler options in the V0 to V2 range. Old-school, face-and-flake style climbing suits the wall, and the long traverse across it is the best-known line, getting plenty of traffic. Flagstaff stone in general is abrasive on the skin, so expect a tough day on the fingertips.

co_southwest_tr.blurb: A short top-rope face on the south side of Gold Butte, a local crag just outside Aspen at a little under 8,000 feet, with views over Buttermilk and the Roaring Fork valley. Eleven routes sit here, mostly 50 to 70 feet long and clustered around 5.8 and 5.9, with a few that reach into the 5.10 range, so it works well for newer climbers and for laps. Anchors are typically built from slings and your own gear along the trail on top, and the walk-off is easy. Mornings get sun; afternoons fall into shade.

co_right_gully.blurb: The gully on the right flank of Blob Rock in Boulder Canyon, between the main Blob and East Blob. It is where much of the hard sport climbing on the formation lives: eleven routes, nearly all of them 5.11 to 5.13, with a handful of two-pitch trad lines mixed in. Expect steep, demanding single-pitch climbing rather than anything for a first-time lead climber. The trail from the roadside pullout swings around to the right of the main wall and climbs up into the gully. The upper east face sits above a large chockstone inside it.
co_right_gully.parking_note: Leave the car at the small pullout on the canyon road just beyond Cob Rock, where the trail up to Blob Rock begins.

co_window_rock_2.blurb: A granite fin near Fall River Road on the west side of Estes Park, named for the window-shaped hole through its middle. It sees little traffic compared with the nearby Lumpy Ridge crags. Eleven climbs here are mostly single-pitch trad, with a couple of bolted sport lines and two aid routes, plus one or two longer outings. Difficulty ranges from an easy 5.7 up through the 5.10s to a few 5.11 and 5.12 lines, so there is something for mid-grade trad climbers. The rock is mostly solid but can be grainy or loose in spots, and summer storms build quickly in the afternoon.
